key_insight: Mixed IQP-QCBMs stay locally trainable while becoming more expressive, but they only outperform ancilla-free IQP models when their branches learn distinct modes of the target distribution.
engineering_relevance: For quantum generative modeling, cluster-based initialization offers a practical way to improve optimization and target multimodal data with less risk of barren-plateau behavior.
method: Generalize ancilla-extended IQP circuits into a weighted mixture of multiple ancilla-free branches.
Prove local barren-plateau avoidance for polynomially many branches under data-agnostic and some data-dependent initializations.
Introduce cluster initialization to assign different unsupervised data clusters to different branches, encouraging mode separation.
evidence_signal: Exact calculations on two 16-bit datasets and experiments on four benchmarks show cluster initialization converges fastest and achieves the lowest mean test MMD^2.
watch_item: Mode separation is difficult when branches start from nearly identical distributions, so the method may require careful initialization and may not scale trivially to harder multimodal data.
paper_title: Trainability and Mode Separation of Mixed IQP-QCBMs
